summary.en: Severe earthquakes have collapsed buildings in Venezuela, creating immediate humanitarian needs. The United States has lifted sanctions on the leader of Venezuela's National Assembly and deployed Space Force electromagnetic and electronic warfare systems against the country. President Nicolás Maduro and his wife face a delayed U.S. torture conspiracy trial scheduled for 2027. A Dutch security report warns that Venezuela's instability could threaten Curaçao and the wider Caribbean Kingdom. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2007, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Alvorlige jordskjelv har kollapset bygninger i Venezuela, noe som skaper umiddelbare humanitære behov. USA har opphevet sanksjoner mot lederen av Venezuelas nasjonalforsamling og har distribuert Space Force elektromagnetiske og elektroniske krigssystemer mot landet. President Nicolás Maduro og hans kone står overfor en utsatt amerikansk torturkonspirasjonsrettssak som er planlagt til 2027. En nederlandsk sikkerhetsrapport advarer om at Venezuelas ustabilitet kan true Curaçao og det bredere Karibiske kongeriket. To dødsfall i kamp ble registrert i 2007, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Crisis in Venezuela
background.extract: An ongoing socioeconomic and political crisis began in Venezuela during the presidencies of Hugo Chávez, Nicolás Maduro and Delcy Rodríguez. It has been marked by hyperinflation, starvation, disease, crime, and mortality rates, resulting in massive emigration. Food shortages and hyperinflation have ended, but inflation remains high. It is the worst economic crisis in Venezuela's history and considered by some sources as more severe than the Great Depression in the United States, the 1985–1994 Brazilian economic crisis, or the 2008–2009 hyperinflation in Zimbabwe. In 2019, the Institute of International Finance called it the single largest economic collapse outside of war in 45 years. Writers have compared aspects, such as unemployment and GDP contraction, to Bosnia and Herzegovina after the 1992–95 Bosnian War, and those in Russia, Cuba and Albania following the Revolutions of 1989.
